newsitem.title: USA: Snowstorm causes headaches in U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Snowstorm causes headaches in U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Heavy snow shut dozens of schools across the Kansas City area Monday in a storm that spread winter misery across parts of the Midwest.

Freezing rain caused hazardous travel in the central part of Missouri and forecasters said 19 states eastward in a band stretching across Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania and on to New England were under winter storm watches.

In the Kansas City area, a morning sleet storm gave way to snow, making roads treacherous. Local meteorologists said six to eight inches of snow would likely fall in eastern Kansas and western Missouri, and that bitter cold temperatures would follow.
Officials in North Dakota reported that the severe winter has even driven some wildlife south.

As many as 38,000 Canadian geese and 68,000 mallards usually flock along the Missouri River in the winter but game experts said they found only 150 geese and 1,500 mallards in a recent survey. Many flew southward looking for open water after the river froze.

Temperatures near or below zero were commonplace in the upper Midwest again Monday and forecasters said the frigid air would slip southward after the storm moves east. At mid-day it was minus 20 in much of North Dakota. Waterloo, Iowa, reported 11.
